profiles.meeting_scenario: The State Coastal Resilience Office and the Metro Community Resilience Coalition are holding a coordination meeting about a new "Preparedness Principles" packet that will be used ahead of hurricane season. The state office has been synthesizing disaster research into a practical guide on preparation, communications, and organizational coordination, while the coalition is responsible for getting the materials in front of local partners before a regional exercise cycle. The immediate agenda is to align on the handoff of materials, which partner network will receive them, what version is being shared this week, and how the materials will support the upcoming exercise activities. The expected outcome is that both participants leave believing they have a clear plan for who sends what, to whom, and by Friday.

members.name: Elena Park
members.role: Regional Preparedness Program Manager, State Coastal Resilience Office
members.expertise: Interagency emergency planning, exercise coordination, grant reporting, state-local preparedness frameworks
members.background: Elena has spent nine years in state emergency management, moving from county planning into regional coordination; she is comfortable with formal planning cycles, version control, and working with agency and VOAD leadership.
members.private_state: She wants the coalition to help socialize the principles quickly so her office can show visible progress before the governor's seasonal readiness briefing, but she also wants to avoid reopening content debates or slowing down the planning timeline with extra review loops.
hidden_assumptions: "Final draft" means the content is substantively locked after internal planning review, even if legal, branding, and accessibility cleanup are still pending.
When someone says "partner list," they usually mean the standing state spreadsheet of county emergency managers and designated VOAD leads.
"The exercise" naturally refers to the June 12 multi-agency tabletop planning session because that is the next formal milestone on her calendar.
A "packet" for circulation can be just the guide PDF plus links to appendices, since downstream groups often build their own outreach wrappers.

members.name: David Mensah
members.role: Preparedness Network Coordinator, Metro Community Resilience Coalition
members.expertise: Community partner engagement, volunteer network coordination, multilingual outreach, NGO logistics
members.background: David came from humanitarian NGO operations and now coordinates a coalition of neighborhood nonprofits, school partners, faith networks, and local service providers involved in preparedness messaging and volunteer mobilization.
members.private_state: He wants usable materials early enough to brief community-facing partners before attention shifts to summer operations, and he is trying to avoid another rollout where local groups receive materials that later change or are too formal to use directly.
hidden_assumptions: "Final draft" means fully cleared for external sharing, including branding, accessibility formatting, and no expected wording changes.

When someone mentions the "partner list," they usually mean the coalition CRM segment for preparedness partners, which includes schools, faith groups, food banks, and neighborhood organizations beyond formal response agencies.
"The exercise" refers to the July 10 regional community tabletop because that is the event for which his network is actively recruiting participants.
If a team says it will send "the packet," that normally includes the guide, a short slide deck, talking points, and any one-page handout needed for partner briefings.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Elena will send the "final draft" this week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this means the guide's substance is fixed enough to hand off, though legal review, ADA formatting, and minor wording changes may still happen afterward.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this means the document is fully approved for outside circulation and stable enough to forward directly to community partners without later revisions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination meetings, "final draft" sounds like ordinary workflow shorthand; both participants are experienced and cooperative, so neither expects the phrase to hide different release thresholds.

misalignment_points.topic: Which "partner list" will receive the materials
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss sending the packet to the "partner list" after the handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the state-maintained spreadsheet of county emergency managers, public information officers, and named VOAD leads used for formal preparedness coordination.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the coalition's preparedness distribution list in its CRM, which includes community-based organizations, school districts, faith leaders, and food access partners.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both organizations maintain an established list commonly called the partner list, and because each list overlaps partially, the phrase feels specific enough to neither person to trigger clarification.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as "ready for the exercise"
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the materials should be "ready for the exercise" by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks readiness means agency participants can review the principles before the June 12 planning tabletop, even if the materials are not yet polished for broad public-facing use.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks readiness means community participants can use the materials ahead of the July 10 regional exercise, which requires clearer formatting and a more accessible briefing package.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There are two exercise-related events in the same workstream, and each is salient to one participant; because both simply say "the exercise," the shared phrase creates false alignment around timing and quality expectations.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to handing off "the packet" for circulation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the packet is the 12-page guide PDF with appendix links, since supporting brief materials can be developed later or locally.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the packet includes the guide plus a two-slide briefing deck, one-page talking points, and a short summary handout needed for community partner calls.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both see the packet as a routine bundle of materials rather than a design decision, each silently fills in the missing components based on their own organization's standard practice.

And the packet can just be the guide PDF with appendix links; we can always add wrappers later if someone wants them.
